review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position. Organizational Context and Scope The forced return of Brazilians represents a significant humanitarian, social, and economic challenge, requiring a coordinated response based on human rights and sustainable reintegration of forced returnees. Many arrive in Brazil in situations of extreme vulnerability, without financial resources, housing, immediate access to essential services, and with significant mental health consequences for directly affected individuals. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Brazil has been implementing a project to support the Brazilian government in ensuring that forcibly returned Brazilian citizens are received with dignity, that their human rights are respected, and that they receive support to overcome vulnerabilities and reintegrate into society. Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the National Project Officer based in Brasilia, the Project Coordinator will be responsible for oversight and overall support in the state of Minas Gerais of the project related to forcibly returnees. Responsibilities In coordination with the National Project Officer based in Brasilia, direct and coordinate the implementation of the project in Lagoa Santa, Minas Gerais; monitor implementation of the field activities to ensure work is proceeding according to established plans; analyze field implementation difficulties and make recommendations for adjusting implementation modalities and work plans to best reflect the changing environment on the field. Regularly research, follow-up, compile, analyze and present information/data on national, regional and international developments, reports, legislation and other relevant documentation regarding forced return and deportation, highlighting noteworthy issues for the consideration of appropriate parties. Liaise and engage with local projects’ partners, and relevant stakeholders in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais. Participate in meetings and conferences indicated by the National Project Officer based in Brasilia; maintain effective liaison and coordination with local authorities, partners, United Nations agencies, intergovernmental and non-governmental organizations, donors, and other stakeholders relevant to the projects. Elaborate internal and external reports, project updates, official documents, press briefing notes, and other related publications; write interim/final narrative reports of the implemented projects for donors. Identify and document good practices and lessons learned; contribute to the development of Standard Operations Procedures (SOP), policies and concept papers and support the development of new projects Perform other work-related tasks, as required. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education High school diploma with a minimum of eight (8) years of relevant professional experience. University degree in social sciences, political sciences, psychology law, public policy, health or a related field from an accredited academic institution with a minimum of three (3) years of experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Working experience in migration context; Experience in project management, including managing projects with Government or UN agency, civil society, regional or international organization; Thorough knowledge of IOM mandate and activities carried out in the current migration context in Brazil; Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, nongovernment or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage; Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations; Experience with movement operations and migrant support is highly advantageous; Knowledge of IOM’s policies and procedures is highly advantageous. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. review_candidates.title: Postdoctoral Fellow – Retinal Biology, Usher Syndrome, and Translational Genomics
review_candidates.description: Site: Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham. Job Summary Will conduct independent and collaborative research, contributing to the advancement of knowledge and the development of innovative solutions. The fellow will work under the supervision of the Principal Investigator and collaborate with a team of researchers. Does this position require Patient Care? No Essential Functions Design, plan, and execute research experiments or projects in alignment with departmental goals. Gather, analyze, and interpret data using appropriate statistical methods and tools. Conduct comprehensive literature reviews to inform research direction and methodologies. Prepare and publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present at conferences and seminars. Work collaboratively with faculty, students, and other researchers, contributing to a positive research environment. Mentor graduate and undergraduate students, providing guidance on research methodologies and techniques. Assist in the preparation of grant proposals and funding applications to support ongoing research. Prepare periodic reports and documents summarizing research progress and outcomes. Qualifications Education Doctorate Related Field of Study required Can this role accept experience in lieu of a degree? No Licenses and Credentials Experience Previous Research experience 3-5 years required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities Demonstrated experience in research techniques, methods, or research areas relevant to the project. Proficient analytical skills, proficiency in statistical software, and excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team. Good interpersonal and communication skills. Salary Range - $71,750.00 - $73,544.00/Annual Additional Job Details (if Applicable) Eaton-Peabody Laboratories, Mass Eye and Ear Harvard Medical School, Boston, Massachusetts The Indzhykulian Laboratory at Mass Eye and Ear/Harvard Medical School is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral fellow to lead and coordinate a collaborative research program investigating the retinal biology of Usher syndrome and advancing the development of therapeutic approaches for inherited sensory disorders. The project brings together investigators with expertise and existing datasets spanning human retina, human retinal organoids, and multiple animal models. The initial goal is to define the therapeutically relevant expression and isoform usage of Usher syndrome genes in the human retina, place these findings in comparative animal context, and establish experimentally supported priorities for retinal cell targeting and therapeutic development. A major component of the project will involve integrating published and unpublished data generated by multiple collaborating laboratories, identifying areas of agreement and discrepancy across datasets and experimental models, and designing targeted experiments to resolve the most important remaining questions. The work is intended to provide a biological foundation for the development and evaluation of gene-replacement, genome-editing, and other therapeutic strategies for Usher syndrome. The successful candidate will work in the Indzhykulian laboratory while interacting closely with a multidisciplinary group of collaborators at Massachusetts Eye and Ear, Harvard-affiliated institutions, and other research centers in the United States and internationally. Responsibilities The postdoctoral fellow will take a central role in the scientific and day-to-day coordination of the project. Responsibilities will include: Integrating and critically evaluating retinal gene-expression and transcript/isoform data from multiple laboratories and experimental systems. Working with computational collaborators to analyze single-cell, bulk, and long-read transcriptomic datasets, with particular attention to cell-type-specific expression and isoform usage of genes associated with Usher syndrome. Comparing findings across human retina, retinal organoids, and relevant animal models to determine which systems best reproduce therapeutically important aspects of human retinal biology. Designing and performing targeted validation experiments in collaboration with participating laboratories, potentially including RNAscope/in situ hybridization, immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, quantitative imaging, and studies in human retinal tissue and retinal organoids. Evaluating the specificity and suitability of antibodies and other reagents for protein-localization studies. Coordinating data exchange and experimental activities among participating laboratories and maintaining an integrated record of results across the collaboration. Presenting findings to collaborators, helping establish project milestones and priorities, and following up on discrepancies or unresolved questions. Taking a leading role in preparation of collaborative manuscripts integrating existing and newly generated data. Contributing to the development of subsequent studies of Usher syndrome retinal biology and therapeutic approaches. Qualifications Applicants should have a PhD, MD/PhD, MD with substantial research training, or equivalent doctoral degree in neuroscience, vision science, molecular/cellular biology, genetics, bioinformatics, or a related discipline. Experience in one or more of the following areas is particularly desirable: Retinal biology or retinal disease Human retinal tissue or iPSC-derived retinal organoids Single-cell or bulk transcriptomic analysis Transcript/isoform analysis, including long-read sequencing RNAscope or other RNA-localization approaches Immunofluorescence and confocal microscopy Quantitative image analysis Molecular genetics or inherited retinal disease R, Python, or related computational/data-analysis approaches The candidate is not expected to have expertise in all of these areas . Of particular importance are scientific curiosity, critical thinking, strong organizational and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively across multiple laboratories and disciplines. The position is particularly well suited to a researcher interested in combining experimental retinal biology with genomic data analysis and translational therapeutic development. Because this project involves contributions from numerous collaborating groups, the successful candidate should be comfortable taking scientific ownership of a complex project while working collaboratively with investigators from different disciplines and institutions. Research Environment The Indzhykulian Laboratory is part of the Eaton-Peabody Laboratories at Mass Eye and Ear and Harvard Medical School. Our laboratory studies the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying sensory function and disease, with a major focus on auditory neuroscience, inner-ear hair-cell biology, and the development of gene therapies and other therapeutic approaches for inherited and acquired forms of deafness. A particular area of interest is Usher syndrome, which provides an opportunity to extend our work on sensory-cell biology and therapeutic development across both the auditory and visual systems. This position will lead the retinal component of this expanding research program and will provide an opportunity to work at the interface of retinal biology, auditory neuroscience, human genetics, genomics, and therapeutic development. The successful candidate will interact with investigators across Mass Eye and Ear, Harvard-affiliated institutions, and a broader network of collaborators with expertise in human retina, retinal organoids, animal models, inherited retinal disease, auditory neuroscience, and gene therapy. The position is available pending finalization of funding and institutional approvals. We work across incredible global industries, delivering exciting work that is defining our future and making an important societal impact in the communities we serve. Our people power our performance – we succeed when they do. With countless opportunities to collaborate, learn, and grow, the possibilities for excellence are as varied as every individual. Whether you want to grow as a subject matter expert or broaden your experience with roles across our international community, you’re surrounded by global specialists who want to combine their expertise and champion you to be your best. As a proudly employee-owned business, we benefit our clients, our communities, and each other, investing in creating the right space for everyone to feel empowered, included, and valued. Whatever your ambition, Mott MacDonald is where people come to be brilliant. About The Business Unit We help conceive, drive, and implement transport solutions for cities, regions, and asset owners/operators around the globe. From preparing the business case and advising on related issues - such as revenue, procurement, and environmental legislation - to delivering the completed infrastructure and helping maintain it. Our planning, engineering, environmental and management skills cover the whole project cycle. We play a major role in developing and delivering the Global Transport Sector Strategy. Overview Of The Role We are looking for a Major Project Director with a track record of delivering complex multi-disciplinary projects from concept design through to Detailed Design to join our Unit. You will be accountable for project team leadership and overall project delivery for multi-million-pound fees on major transport and civil infrastructure projects. You will lead the planning and delivery stages of infrastructure works for clients and be responsible for the technical quality of reliable design solutions. You’ll play a leading role in client engagement and preparing bids to secure future major project opportunities that will deliver our ambitious growth targets whilst meeting the objectives of our clients and their customers. Additionally, as an integral and senior member of the team, you’ll contribute to the Unit’s business planning strategy and team’s professional development. Key responsibilities and duties include: Leading profitable projects that deliver successful outcomes for our clients and communities Implementing a collaborative and integrated delivery approach across project teams, supply chain, partners, and client teams Delivering to budget, programme, and quality Enhancing client satisfaction Undertaking Project Reviews to foster continuous improvement and sharing lessons across projects In this role, you’ll be accountable for: Championing industry leading techniques to improve safety and customer service to deliver the goals of our clients and their customers Delivery of projects to time, cost, and quality Fostering innovation in the delivery of design, digital and technical excellence Delivering client requirements and customer satisfaction Candidate specification Essential: Extensive experience of delivering major design projects in the project director role (design fees of greater than £5m), especially under a Design & Build contract form Project, financial, programme and resource management skills Management / directing large project teams (over 100 people) Ability to deliver to demanding schedules and targets Proven business development and marketing skills with demonstrable experience of writing winning proposals Excellent communication skills to be able to communicate targets, and priorities to staff, clients and partners BEng / BSc civil engineering (or related subject) Chartered Engineer (or equivalent) Member of the Institution of Engineers Ireland (or equivalent) We offer some fantastic benefits including: Flexible working Pension matched up to 7% of base salary Competitive annual leave An annual professional institution subscription Life insurance Income continuance Enhanced Paternity leave Annual company performance bonus scheme – Subject to company performance Cycle to work scheme Travel TaxSaver tickets Commitment to Continuing Professional Development – we are accredited by Engineers Ireland Mentoring and support for career development and progression Employee Ownership Our employee ownership model means no external investors, just us, creating a culture of shared success. Our employees have a stake and a voice in our business, giving them a direct connection to our success through our personal and group performance bonuses. As your career grows, so does your stake, recognising your long-term impact and contribution. Your voice matters, with the opportunity to connect directly with senior leadership through formal channels to help shape our future. For our senior roles you will have a direct pathway towards ownership from day one. Equality, diversity, and inclusion We put equality, diversity, and inclusion at the heart of our business, seeking to promote fair employment procedures and practices to ensure equal opportunities for all. We encourage individual expression in our workplace and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels they can contribute. AI Usage At Mott MacDonald, we see the value AI can bring, but we take a people-first approach to hiring. While AI tools can help candidates prepare and build confidence, every application and hiring decision is reviewed by our recruitment and hiring teams. We encourage the responsible use of AI while ensuring we get to know the real person behind the application. Accessibility We want you to feel supported and able to perform at your best throughout our recruitment process. If there is anything we can do to make applying or interviewing with us more accessible, please contact us at reasonable.adjustments@mottmac.com and we'll be happy to discuss how we can help. Agile working At Mott MacDonald, we believe it makes business sense for you and your manager to choose how you can work most effectively to meet your client, team, and personal commitments. We offer a hybrid working policy that embraces your well-being, flexibility, and trust. Apply now, or for more information about our application process, click here. review_candidates.title: Logistics & Inventory Coordinator
review_candidates.description: College Group are a privately held company founded in 1989. We are the largest processor and exporter of animal by-products in Ireland. Diversification and investment strategy has resulted in large scale developments in the production of biofuels and the manufacture of organic fertilisers. Continuous development has led to expansion into renewable energy with solar installation and renewable gas production with our AD Plant. We are currently seeking to recruit a Logistics & Inventory Coordinator for College Biofuels Plant in Nobber. The Logistics & Inventory Coordinator is responsible for coordinating inbound and outbound deliveries, maintaining accurate stock and inventory records, and supporting the smooth operation of the production facility. The role is focused on coordinating inbound raw materials and outbound finished goods, ensuring continuity of supply to production and the timely fulfilment of customer orders. Responsibilities include tracking deliveries and shipments, scheduling dispatches, maintaining accurate stock and inventory records, and working closely with suppliers, customers, hauliers and site personnel to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of logistics activities. The successful candidate will be highly organised, methodical and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment managing delivery schedules, inventory information and operational data. A key aspect of the role is ensuring that stock, logistics and ordering information is accurately maintained and readily accessible to the wider business. TASKS Operate and monitor the site weighbridge, ensuring all deliveries and dispatches are accurately recorded. Coordinate inbound and outbound deliveries of raw materials and finished products. Schedule, track and monitor deliveries arriving by tanker, ISO tank and container. Liaise with suppliers, hauliers, freight forwarders, customs agents and site personnel to ensure timely deliveries and collections. Monitor shipments and follow up on delayed or outstanding deliveries. Support customs clearance activities and ensure import documentation is completed accurately and on time. Monitor port-held containers and coordinate collection to avoid unnecessary storage, demurrage and related charges. Manage raw material ordering and maintain appropriate inventory levels to support production requirements. Maintain accurate stock records and investigate any discrepancies in deliveries, inventory or documentation. Produce stock control, inventory, utility usage and logistics reports. Maintain clear and effective administrative systems, records and processes. Support general office and facility administration activities. Experience Previous experience in logistics, stock control or other similar process-driven roles. Good numerical ability and attention to detail. Comfortable working with spreadsheets, reports and business systems. Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a structured manner. Calm and methodical approach in a busy office environment. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Proactive attitude with a willingness to take ownership of tasks and follow them through to completion.

review_candidates.description: FICHTNER - Engineering for a better tomorrow Seit über 100 Jahren steht Fichtner als unabhängiges Familienunternehmen für Verlässlichkeit, Integrität und eine werteorientierte Unternehmenskultur. Als Ingenieur- und Beratungsunternehmen arbeiten wir an Lösungen für die großen Themen unserer Zeit – von Energie und Umwelt bis zur Digitalisierung. Unsere Projekte verbinden technische Exzellenz mit gesellschaftlicher Relevanz und bieten Ihnen die Möglichkeit, wirklich etwas zu bewegen. In internationalen und interdisziplinären Teams profitieren wir von unterschiedlichen Perspektiven – und schaffen so hochwertige, passgenaue Lösungen für unsere Kunden. Sie erwartet ein Arbeitsumfeld, das von Vertrauen, Eigenverantwortung und klaren Zielen geprägt ist. Wir schaffen Orientierung und übertragen Verantwortung – und bieten Ihnen gleichzeitig die Freiräume, Ihre Stärken wirksam einzubringen und sich kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln. Aufgaben Sie sind Teil eines fachlichen Planungsteams für große, linienförmige Infrastrukturprojekte (Erdkabel sowie Gas- und Wasserstoff-Pipelines). Entwurfsplanung im Bereich Grabenbau, Tiefbau und Spezialtiefbau (HDD, Microtunnel, Bohrpressverfahren) Interpretation von geologischen und geotechnischen Unterlagen Integration von umweltfachlichen, genehmigungsrelevanten und anderen technischen Unterlagen Mitwirkung bei der Trassenplanung vom Entwurf bis zur Ausführung Zusammenarbeit im Projektteam bei Bauablaufplanung, Terminplanung, Kostenmanagement und Risikomanagement sowie Qualitätskontrolle Profil Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium (Uni/FH) im Bereich Bauingenieurwesen, Geotechnik oder vergleichbar. Alternativ eine vergleichbare, durch langjährige Berufserfahrung gewonnene Qualifikation Wünschenswert ist (erste) Berufserfahrung im Bereich Erdbau-, Tiefbau oder vergleichbaren Bereichen Sehr gutes technisches Verständnis und Interesse am Erwerben neuer Fachkenntnisse Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Regulierungs- und Genehmigungsbehörden von Vorteil Kenntnisse in CAD und Spezialsoftware, z.B. Plaxis, GeoStudio oder GGU sind vorteilhaft Sehr gute Kenntnisse in den gängigen MS Office-Produkten Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse Sehr gute Kommunikationsfähigkeit und ein hoher Grad an Eigeninitiative Wir bieten Damit Sie Ihr Potenzial im Projektumfeld von Fichtner voll entfalten können, bieten wir Ihnen: Langfristigkeit & Perspektive: Sie profitieren von der Stabilität und Verlässlichkeit eines unabhängigen Familienunternehmens sowie von langfristigen Perspektiven und individuellen Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten. Verantwortung & Flexibilität: In Ihrer Arbeit genießen Sie hohe Freiheitsgrade und Eigenverantwortung. Zudem bieten wir Ihnen ein flexibles Gleitzeitmodell und 30 Urlaubstage (bei Vollzeitanstellung). Modernes Arbeiten: Wir stellen Ihnen eine moderne digitale Infrastruktur für mobiles und flexibles Arbeiten zur Verfügung. Entwicklung & Lernen: Durch eine strukturierte Einarbeitung und regelmäßige Weiterbildungsangebote fördern wir Ihre persönliche und fachliche Entwicklung gezielt. Mobilität: Wir unterstützen Ihre Mobilität mit einem Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket, Job-Rad-Leasing sowie unseren gut erreichbaren Standorten. Gesundheit & Ausgleich: Ein E-Gym Wellpass sowie ein breites Angebot an Firmen- und Sportaktivitäten tragen zu Ihrer Gesundheit und Ihrem Ausgleich bei. Miteinander & Unternehmenskultur: An unserem Standort in Stuttgart können Sie unsere Betriebskantine nutzen, während wir an anderen Standorten digitale Essensangebote bereitstellen. Unsere regelmäßigen Team- und Firmenevents stärken den Zusammenhalt. Wenn Sie Teil unseres Teams werden möchten, bewerben Sie sich einfach in wenigen Schritten über unser Portal. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung! Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE
